fixes.explanation: Right, baker. The text says, "For he thought, “Will there not at least be peace and security in my lifetime?”" (2 Kings 20:19) That's the thought the verse gives right alongside his reply. It's the thought behind the words he says to Isaiah.
Manasseh, baker. The verse says, "…his son Manasseh reigned in his place." (2 Kings 20:21) Hezekiah rested with his fathers, and the throne passed to his son. That wraps up the story of Hezekiah.

The text doesn't say the letters held a warning, baker. It says Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift (2 Kings 20:12). It never gives what the letters said. The word that comes later in this passage comes from Isaiah the prophet.

The text doesn't mention a summons, baker. It says Merodach-baladan, king of Babylon, sent letters and a gift (2 Kings 20:12). It never gives what the letters said. The gift is the part the verse names, and nobody opens a gift hoping it's a court date.

Trading is a fine idea, but it's not what the text says. The reason given is that the king of Babylon "…had heard about Hezekiah’s illness." (2 Kings 20:12) Trade isn't mentioned anywhere in that verse.

The text doesn't say what the guests asked to see, baker. It says Hezekiah showed them "…all that was found in his storehouses." (2 Kings 20:13) He was the one giving this tour. The verse says, "There was nothing in his palace or in all his dominion that Hezekiah did not show them."

That's what he says, baker. Hezekiah answers Isaiah, "The word of the LORD that you have spoken is good." (2 Kings 20:19) It's a surprising thing to say right after hearing that. The rest of that verse tells us what he was thinking.
Josiah is a fine name, but it's not the one here, baker. The verse says, "…his son Manasseh reigned in his place." (2 Kings 20:21) Manasseh is the son who takes the throne after Hezekiah.
Jotham isn't the son named in this verse, friend. It says, "…his son Manasseh reigned in his place." (2 Kings 20:21) Manasseh took the throne after Hezekiah rested with his fathers.
